## Slide 1 — Title

**Ten-step approach:** One way of setting up a topical working group to promote the transition to a circular economy

(Or a "Transition Group")

## Slide 2 — The Ten-Step Methodology for Transition Groups (overview)

1. Mandate, North Star and Success Criteria (TG Charter)
2. Problem Framing and Scoping (Nordic Case for Change)
3. Stakeholder and Commitment Mapping
4. Mobilisation and Communication
5. Operating Model for the Transition Group
6. Insight, Baseline and Selection of Transition Levers
7. Co-Design and Pilot Portfolio
8. White Paper as Engine
9. Gate Evaluation and Consolidation (Go / Iterate / Pause)
10. Implementable Roadmap (1–3 Years)

## Slide 3 — Step 1: Mandate, North Star and Success Criteria (TG Charter)

- Establish a clear one-page charter that defines why the Transition Group exists, what it aims to achieve, and how success will be measured.
- *In practice:* Draft a charter covering purpose, goals, scope and non-scope, success metrics/KPIs, and roles.
- Inspired by **PRINCE2/PMI project charter governance** and **RACI responsibility mapping**.

## Slide 4 — Step 2: Problem Framing and Scoping

- Sharpen the problem definition and articulate why this challenge needs to be addressed at a Nordic level, right now.
- *In practice:* Develop a precise problem statement, a "why Nordic, why now" rationale, and a set of prioritised transition hypotheses.
- Draws on **Design Thinking / Double Diamond (Define phase)** and **Theory of Change** impact logic.

## Slide 5 — Step 3: Stakeholder and Commitment Mapping

- Identify which actors must be on board for the group to deliver real impact, and clarify what is being asked of each one.
- *In practice:* Build a prioritised stakeholder map paired with a specific "ask" for every actor.
- Based on **Bryson's stakeholder analysis** and **Kotter's guiding coalition** concept.

## Slide 6 — Step 4: Mobilisation and Communication

- Invite the right people in with a low-threshold offer that makes participation easy and attractive.
- *In practice:* Produce an invitation plan and a **"commitment light" package** — typically *one meeting, one page, two contacts, one concrete action*.
- Grounded in **Kotter's communicate-and-mobilise stage** and strategic communication practice (e.g. **FirstHouse**).

## Slide 7 — Step 5: Operating Model for the Transition Group

- Define the rhythm, roles and working artefacts that will keep the group productive over time.
- *In practice:* Set up meeting cadence, sprint plan, decision log, document structure, and short retrospectives.
- Inspired by **Agile/Scrum cadence** and a **lightweight OKR approach** with few, clear goals.

## Slide 8 — Step 6: Insight, Baseline and Selection of Transition Levers

- Build a shared understanding of the current state and choose which levers the group will actually pull to drive change.
- *In practice:* Produce an as-is insight note, system map, and bottleneck analysis, then select transition levers across **policy, procurement, standards, finance, data and tracking, infrastructure, and competence**.
- Combines **systems thinking**, **Results-Based Management baselines**, and **OECD evidence practice**.

## Slide 9 — Step 7: Co-Design and Pilot Portfolio

- Translate insight into action by co-designing a focused portfolio of pilots with clear ownership.
- *In practice:* Develop **2–5 pilot proposals**, an associated **requirements/standards track**, and an **owner map**.
- Draws on **Design Thinking (Develop phase)**, **Lean Startup (MVP/pilot)**, and **portfolio thinking**.

## Slide 10 — Step 8: White Paper as Engine

- Use a citable white paper to drive the policy, market and standards narrative forward.
- *In practice:* Produce a citable white paper, a one-page executive brief, and a set of recommended levers.
- Built on **McKinsey-style structured problem-solution communication** and established **policy brief practice**.

## Slide 11 — Step 9: Gate Evaluation and Consolidation

- Pause to evaluate progress, capture learning, and decide whether to continue, adjust or stop.
- *In practice:* Produce a learning note and a documented decision on the next phase, partners, and prioritised tracks.
- Based on **OECD DAC criteria** (relevance, effectiveness, impact) and **After Action Review** methodology.

## Slide 12 — Step 10: Implementable Roadmap (1–3 Years)

- Convert the work into an actionable roadmap with financing and an adoption pathway across the Nordics.
- *In practice:* Deliver a roadmap covering actions, owners, milestones, resources/financing, risks, KPIs, and a **standardisation and adoption plan**.
- Combines **roadmapping practice**, **PRINCE2 benefits management**, and **ISO 31000 risk management**.

## Diff vs Cathrine v2.0 (research/cathrine-ten-step-oppsummering.md)

JT Tallinn-versjonen er **NCH-bredt cross-sector** og bruker andre metodikk-referanser enn Cathrines Food-TG-spesifikke v2.0. Ikke motstridende — komplementære lag.

| Steg | Cathrine v2.0 (Food TG) | JT Tallinn 2026-05-06 (NCH cross-sector) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | + 10R (Wageningen), ISO 59000, ESRS 1-5, NCH sektor/system-dim | Ren PRINCE2/PMI + RACI |
| 2 | + PESTEL per land | Design Thinking/Double Diamond + Theory of Change |
| 3 | Bryson + Kotter | Bryson + Kotter (likt) |
| 4 | Kotter + Nordic Innovation Playbooks | + **FirstHouse**, "commitment light" = 1 møte / 1 side / 2 kontakter / 1 konkret action |
| 5 | Agile sprint + RACI + Gate A inline (uke 2) | Agile/Scrum + **lightweight OKR** + retros |
| 6 | Strategyzer BME, MFA/LCA, Eurostat sirkulærmonitor, ISO 59020, "fem sløyfer" | + **Results-Based Management baselines**, **OECD evidence**, transition levers (policy/procurement/standards/finance/data/infra/kompetanse) |
| 7 | Ellen MacArthur/IDEO + Cambridge CE + runde-4 P1-aktørliste | + **Lean Startup MVP** + **portfolio thinking** + requirements/standards track |
| 8 | Theory of Change + evidence-based policy brief | + **McKinsey structured problem-solution** + executive brief |
| 9 | Stage-gate + mini-retro + **Transition Factor test** + Gate B (uke 8) | **OECD DAC** (relevans/effektivitet/impact) + **After Action Review** |
| 10 | Roadmapping + risk/finans/KPI + Minimum Viable Transition (Ownership/Implementation/Institutional/Resourcing) | + **PRINCE2 benefits management** + **ISO 31000 risk management** + standardisation/adoption-plan |

## Anbefalt merge-strategi

JT er **NCH-canonical layer** — referansene (OECD DAC, AAR, ISO 31000, Lean Startup, McKinsey, RBM, FirstHouse, OKR) er det programmet brukes utad.

Cathrine er **Food-TG-spesifikk overlay** — sirkularitetsanker (10R, ISO 59000, ESRS, "fem sløyfer", Strategyzer, Eurostat) + runde-4 valideringsdisiplin.
